title: namchain rig document
description:
The rig document the namchain engine runs: what `rig.apply` accepts, what `rig.get` returns, and what the daemon keeps as its rig file (`last.json`). Source of truth: the parser in namchain src/graph/rig.cpp (`parse_document_json`), which is the contract — it refuses unknown keys at every level except the node, where any key that is not reserved is a parameter.

This is the form ljoss's rig tree is transformed into: the designer document (ljoss-rig.schema.json) is flattened by ljoss's DocumentEncoder into these nodes and connections, then `rig.apply`-ed to the daemon. The app's document stays the tree; this document is a sink, never re-hydrated.

Two accepted shapes, exactly one of them in a document:
1. `chains` — the shape documents use now: named chains, each with its own graph and device channel binding (what ljoss sends).
2. the legacy top-level `nodes`/`connections` — one graph, one chain with id "main" and channels 0/0 (what rigs/guitar-chain.json and older rig files are).

The parser is strict where the designer format is tolerant: an unknown key here is a refused mistake, not ignored. A client's own data has a place — the `meta` object, which the engine carries and never reads.

oneOf.title: chains form
oneOf.description: A document of named chains. A chain binds device channels itself; there is no nc.input/nc.output channel parameter.

oneOf.title: legacy single-graph form
oneOf.description: The shape everything was in before documents existed: one graph, one chain ('main', channels 0 and 0). A compatibility rule, not a special case.

meta.description: The client's own data. Must be an object; the engine stores it and never parses it. Free-form content inside.

node.title: node

id.description: Unique within the chain; what connections and rig.patch name. Optional — if absent the engine mints one from `element` (and `role`).

type.description: The engine type: nc.gain, nc.nam, fx.delay.feedback, … One of the ids engine.schema publishes (namchain-engine-schema.schema.json).

element.description: The client's own identity for the document thing this node came from — ljoss puts a block's or parallel section's UUID here. Stored and returned verbatim; NOT required to be unique (an amp is two nodes sharing one element). At least one of id / element must be present.

role.description: Which node of a macro's lowered graph this is, for element+role addressing (docs/macros.md). The engine's word, not the client's.

bypass.description: A bypassed node keeps running and passes its dry input through, so its state stays warm and un-bypassing does not click. Only allowed on 1→1 nodes.

params.description: Explicit numeric parameters. Inline shorthand keys can still override these.

strings.description: Explicit string parameters (a model or IR name, an option value). Inline shorthand keys can still override these.

anyOf.description: A flag; the parser stores true as 1.0 and false as 0.0.
A string parameter — a library id like a model or IR, or an option value.

node.description: Every key other than the reserved ones (id, type, element, role, params, strings, bypass, meta) is a parameter: a number is a numeric param, a boolean a flag, a string a string param. That is the whole vocabulary — a parameter named like a reserved key cannot exist, which is why ljoss's encoder refuses to produce one.

connection.title: connection

from_port.description: An integer port number; the parser refuses a float, a bool or a string rather than truncating.

connection.description: from → to, by node id, with an optional port on each side. An unconnected input is legal and is bound to silence — a dry lane is a matter of not wiring it.

input_channel.description: Which device channel the chain reads. Lives on the chain, not on nc.input: it is a property of the chain, not of a node.

nodes.description: Node order is irrelevant to the compiler — the connections are the graph.
